faq.q: Do I need to know my future career already?
faq.a: No. Start with your interests and compare several fields. A career choice does not define your whole life; you can refine it with experience.

faq.q: How is this quiz different from a career test?
faq.a: It clarifies your situation and immediate tasks. It is not psychological diagnosis or an assessment of ability. You can explore Ventorme’s career test separately.

faq.q: What will I see after six questions?
faq.a: A main focus, a short explanation and three next actions. The result appears before registration. We do not ask for your name, email or phone number.

faq.q: What happens when I go to Ventorme?
faq.a: The real Ventorme registration page opens. Create an account and complete onboarding there. Your quiz answers are not transferred automatically. Check feature terms on the platform.

faq.q: How should I check subject and exam requirements?
faq.a: Use the official page for each specific programme and your admission year. For IB, check subjects, HL/SL levels and scores. There is no single rule for every university.

direction.title: From interests to fields
direction.why: You want to explore your direction. Begin with real activities and your own criteria.
steps: List 2–3 activities or topics you would like to explore further.
Look at what several careers and study programmes actually involve.
Compare fields using your criteria and choose one to investigate next.
direction.extra: Write down the criteria you will use to compare fields.

universities.title: A university shortlist
universities.why: It helps to narrow the list and compare programmes using the same criteria.
steps: Find 3–5 specific study programmes in your field.
Compare content, teaching language, location and total cost.
Read each programme’s official requirements for your admission year.
universities.extra: Add comparison criteria to your programme shortlist.

subjects.title: Subjects for specific programmes
subjects.why: Requirements differ. Check specific programmes before deciding on school subjects.
steps: Choose a few specific programmes to investigate.
Check subject and exam requirements on their official pages.
Compare them with your curriculum and discuss any gaps with an adviser.
subjects.extra: Check school subjects on official programme pages.

funding.title: A clear picture of costs
funding.why: You want to understand affordability. Compare the full cost and funding conditions.
steps: List tuition, living costs and required expenses for several programmes.
Check official scholarship and grant pages and eligibility conditions.
Record deadlines, documents and missing information for each funding option.
funding.extra: Add total costs and funding conditions to your comparison.

exams.title: Exams in a useful order
exams.why: You want an exam plan. First find out which exams you actually need.
steps: Check required exams and scores on your chosen programmes’ pages.
Compare result release dates with application deadlines.
Assess your starting level and create a realistic preparation plan.
exams.extra: Check required exams before choosing preparation courses.

documents.title: Documents and deadlines together
documents.why: You are preparing applications. Make upcoming deadlines and missing documents visible.
steps: Collect document requirements and upcoming deadlines for each programme.
Make a calendar for applications, exams and recommendations.
Check which documents, translations and essays still need preparation.
documents.extra: List missing documents and their preparation deadlines.

start.title: One clear starting point
start.why: Choosing a first action feels difficult. Start with a short list of open questions.
steps: Write down what you know and what remains unclear.
Choose one field or programme to research first.
Open its official page and identify one small next action.
start.extra: Choose one manageable action for the near future.

ibSteps: Find a few specific programmes in your chosen field.
Check required subjects, HL/SL levels and scores on official pages.
Compare requirements with your current or planned DP subjects and discuss them with your school adviser.
